dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product labels things with a word that is not a control: the category of an article, the state of an order, the stage of a release, the requirement of a field, the value that is the default among several. It draws most of them quietly, some as an outline where a fill would weigh a dense table down, and one filled where it is the chosen one; and it draws a state that is information, a success, a warning or an error in that status's colors, beside the neutral ones.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything a tag reads: for each size, its minimum height, its padding where the label meets an end and where a glyph or a dot does, and the label's text style; the padding above and below, the gap between the mark and the label, the corners; the glyph's and the dot's sizes; the outlined look's edge; and for each look (tonal, outlined, filled), with no status and in each status (info, warning, error, success), the fill, the label's color and the color of the glyph or the dot — at rest, and drawn inside something disabled.
rules: A tag is a static label: it names a category or a status and does nothing. It takes no press, no focus and has no states of its own; inside something disabled it is drawn from its disabled colors (disabled), and nothing else changes. A label that does something is a chip (an action, a filter, a removable value) or a link.
A badge is a count or a dot attached to another element; a tag stands by itself in the layout. Do not use a tag for a count on an icon, or a badge for a word.

Tonal is the default. Use outlined where many tags sit close together (a table column, a list of categories). Use filled for the chosen one among its neighbours, and at most one status per view drawn filled.
A status is never shown by color alone: the label says it ("Failed"), or statusLabel adds it in words for assistive technology ("Error").
A look's tokens carry its name, then the status when it has one: tonal.container.color, tonal.error.container.color.
A product-specific meaning (a brand, a category color) is not one of the four statuses: declare a palette in a layer and add a value to the variant axis; do not reuse error or success for it.
container.height is a minimum: a tag grows with enlarged text.
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never draw a pill by hand.

The requirement tag of a Field and of a field group is this component as it is — small, filled for required, tonal for optional — and reads these tokens: what a layer changes for small tags it changes for the requirement tag, which has no token of its own.

height.$description: A tag's minimum height, per size. Small follows a field's label, a table cell's text or a line of body text without making the line taller; medium stands beside a heading or by itself. Both are under the chip's heights at the same size name (24 and 32), so a tag never has the height of a control it could be taken for.

padding-inline.$description: Padding at an end where the label meets the edge, per size.

padding-inline-with-icon.$description: Padding at the start when a glyph or the dot stands there, per size: tighter than the label's, so the mark aligns optically with a round end.

padding-block.$description: Padding above and below the row's tallest item (the label's line or the glyph's box), per size. Heights are minimums, so this shows only when text is enlarged: one line of each size's text style with this padding is exactly that size's height (16 + 2 × 2 = 20; 20 + 2 × 2 = 24). It is the same at both sizes in the default system and is kept per size because the build checks each height against the padding of its own size.

gap.$description: Distance between the glyph or the dot and the label.

shape.$description: The container's corners, capped at half its height: a pill in the default system, at any height the tag grows to. A product that wants its tags told from its chips by shape sets a step of the corner scale here.

color.$description: The edge of an outlined tag, in every status: the one hairline, the color the divider and an outlined chip draw theirs in. Decorative: the label carries the meaning. It keeps its own token so that a system can draw this edge apart from its dividers.

width.$description: The width of an outlined tag's edge, drawn inside the container's size.

typescale.$description: The label's text style, per size.

size.$description: The box of the leading glyph, at both sizes: the smallest step of the icon scale, which fits the small height with the block padding (16 + 2 × 2 = 20). A tag's glyph is a mark beside a word, not a control's icon.
The diameter of the dot, at both sizes: half the glyph's box, large enough for its color to be seen beside 12 text and small enough to read as a mark, not as a glyph.

color.$description: The quiet fill of a tag that names a category or a neutral state: the tonal role, the fill the text field's optional label has.
The glyph and the dot of a tonal tag with no status: the label's color, because with no status there is nothing for a second color to say.
The fill of a tonal info tag: the status's quiet container, a faint tint of the status on the scheme's surface, the color the snackbar's info form is drawn on.
The glyph and the dot of a tonal info tag: the status's own color, the one chromatic mark on a quiet fill. The label, not this color, says the status.
The fill of a tonal warning tag: the status's quiet container, a faint tint of the status on the scheme's surface, the color the snackbar's warning form is drawn on.
The glyph and the dot of a tonal warning tag: the status's own color, the one chromatic mark on a quiet fill. The label, not this color, says the status.
The fill of a tonal error tag: the status's quiet container, a faint tint of the status on the scheme's surface, the color the snackbar's error form is drawn on.
The glyph and the dot of a tonal error tag: the status's own color, the one chromatic mark on a quiet fill. The label, not this color, says the status.
The fill of a tonal success tag: the status's quiet container, a faint tint of the status on the scheme's surface, the color the snackbar's success form is drawn on.
The glyph and the dot of a tonal success tag: the status's own color, the one chromatic mark on a quiet fill. The label, not this color, says the status.
An outlined tag has no fill: the surface behind shows through, inside the one hairline (outline.color).

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: This variant has no fill; the surface behind shows through.

color.$description: The glyph and the dot of an outlined tag with no status: secondary content, quieter than the label.
No fill, as every outlined tag.
The label of an outlined info tag stays the surface's text color: the status shows in the mark before it (TAG-8), and the edge stays the one hairline.
The glyph and the dot of an outlined info tag: the status's own color, the only place this look shows the status.
No fill, as every outlined tag.
The label of an outlined warning tag stays the surface's text color: the status shows in the mark before it (TAG-8), and the edge stays the one hairline.
The glyph and the dot of an outlined warning tag: the status's own color, the only place this look shows the status.
No fill, as every outlined tag.
The label of an outlined error tag stays the surface's text color: the status shows in the mark before it (TAG-8), and the edge stays the one hairline.
The glyph and the dot of an outlined error tag: the status's own color, the only place this look shows the status.
No fill, as every outlined tag.
The label of an outlined success tag stays the surface's text color: the status shows in the mark before it (TAG-8), and the edge stays the one hairline.
The glyph and the dot of an outlined success tag: the status's own color, the only place this look shows the status.
The fill of the tag that marks the chosen one among its neighbours (the default among values, the required among fields): primary, the fill the text field's required label has.
On a full fill the glyph and the dot take the label's color: a second color would not hold against the fill.
The fill of a filled info tag: the status's own color, for the one status on a screen that must not be missed.
The fill of a filled warning tag: the status's own color, for the one status on a screen that must not be missed.
The fill of a filled error tag: the status's own color, for the one status on a screen that must not be missed.
The fill of a filled success tag: the status's own color, for the one status on a screen that must not be missed.
